Senses.Explanation: A further barrier names an additional gate beyond an earlier passage, commonly in lines about penetrating or emerging through layered barriers. The expression occurs 739 times in 227 allowlisted texts. Counts range from one to ten thousand barriers; one passes, breaks, opens, guards, or remains separated by them. The recurring warning says, ‘do not say no-mind is the Way; no-mind still leaves one further barrier.’ Speakers also ask who has passed it, request presentation of ‘the final barrier,’ and direct a questioner to ‘ask the gatekeeper.’ A late discourse gives its own named description of ‘passing through the further barrier’; this is preserved as that text’s account, not made universal. Zen bends the checkpoint image into a public measure, but the corpus names no fixed numbered stage shared by every use.
